answer: The gale graph is rebuilt each epoch, which means the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the basalt audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 4 times its size, so a group of 94 keys loses far more than 94 single identities would. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the garden checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. That is 30 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
